title: What is DevOps? Culture, automation and delivery explained
seoTitle: What Is DevOps? CI/CD, Automation and Culture Explained
seoDescription: Learn what DevOps means, how CI/CD, infrastructure as code, observability and shared ownership improve software delivery.
excerpt: DevOps is not one tool or job title. It is a way of reducing the friction between building software and operating it reliably.
author: KitsuWire Editorial
keyTakeaways: DevOps combines cultural practices and technical automation to shorten feedback loops between development and operations.
CI/CD, infrastructure as code, observability and automated testing are common enabling practices rather than a complete definition of DevOps.
The goal is faster delivery without treating reliability, security and operations as someone else's problem.
body: Traditional software organizations often separated developers who wrote applications from operations teams who deployed and supported them. That boundary could create slow handoffs, conflicting incentives and poor feedback.
DevOps emerged as a collection of cultural and engineering practices aimed at making delivery and operations a shared system rather than two disconnected phases.

sections.heading: DevOps is more than tooling
paragraphs: Buying a CI server or hiring a DevOps engineer does not automatically create DevOps. The deeper change is shared responsibility, fast feedback and automation of repetitive delivery work.
Teams need visibility into how their software behaves in production and enough ownership to improve both the application and the process that delivers it.

sections.heading: Continuous integration and delivery
paragraphs: Continuous integration encourages developers to merge changes frequently while automated builds and tests provide rapid feedback. Continuous delivery keeps software in a releasable state through a repeatable deployment pipeline.
Automation reduces manual variation, but pipeline quality depends on meaningful tests, secure credentials, reliable environments and clear rollback strategies.

sections.heading: Infrastructure as code
paragraphs: Infrastructure as code expresses infrastructure configuration in version-controlled definitions. Tools such as Terraform can create cloud resources, while configuration-management and platform tools configure systems and applications.
Reviewable definitions make changes more repeatable and auditable than undocumented manual clicks, although state, secrets and lifecycle management still need careful design.

sections.heading: Observability and feedback
paragraphs: Metrics, logs and traces help teams understand production behavior. Alerting should focus attention on conditions that require action rather than creating constant noise.
Operational data also feeds development decisions. If releases increase latency or error rates, teams need a short path from that signal to diagnosis and correction.

sections.heading: DevSecOps and security
paragraphs: Security can be integrated into delivery through dependency scanning, secret detection, image scanning, policy checks and secure defaults. Automation helps move checks earlier without pretending that every security problem can be solved in a pipeline.
Identity, least privilege, threat modeling and incident response remain broader organizational responsibilities.

sections.heading: DevOps and platform engineering
paragraphs: As organizations grow, every team independently building pipelines and Kubernetes platforms creates duplication. Platform engineering can package proven DevOps capabilities into self-service internal products.
A good platform reduces cognitive load while preserving useful developer autonomy. It should make the safe path easier, not simply introduce another ticket queue.

faq.question: Is DevOps a job title?
faq.answer: Organizations use DevOps Engineer as a job title, but DevOps itself describes broader practices and collaboration across software delivery and operations.

faq.question: Is Kubernetes required for DevOps?
faq.answer: No. DevOps practices apply to virtual machines, serverless platforms, containers and many other environments.

faq.question: What is the difference between DevOps and SRE?
faq.answer: They overlap. Site Reliability Engineering applies software-engineering approaches to reliability and defines practices such as service-level objectives and error budgets, while DevOps is a broader delivery and collaboration movement.
